Left: querying edge id 3 finds the accent edge between B and C, so has_edge_id returns True. Right: no edge carries id 9, so has_edge_id returns False." width="100%"} Every edge receives a unique integer ID when it is added. This method reports whether an edge with a particular ID is currently in the graph. Edge IDs are not reused: once an edge is deleted its ID stays retired, and later edges receive fresh IDs. So an ID you stored earlier can go stale, and `has_edge_id()` is how you detect that. Use it to: - validate edge IDs before passing them to methods such as `get_edge()` or `delete_edge_by_id()` - check whether edges recorded earlier (e.g. in a selection or an external table) still exist after the graph has been modified To test whether two nodes are connected without knowing an edge ID, use `has_edge()` instead. The check is against the whole graph and ignores the current selection. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The integer edge ID to look up, as returned by methods like `get_edge_ids()` or `find_edge_ids()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if an edge with this ID exists, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A valid edge ID returns `True`; an ID that was never assigned returns `False`: ::: {#37be8ef5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) edge_id = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.has_edge_id(edge_id=edge_id), graph.has_edge_id(edge_id=9999) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: After an edge is deleted its ID is no longer valid, and a newly added edge gets a fresh ID rather than reusing the old one. Here edge `1` is gone and the new edge is `3`: ::: {#5eba6b21 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.delete_edge(source="A", target="B") graph.add_edge(source="A", target="C") graph.has_edge_id(edge_id=1), graph.get_edge_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (False, [2, 3]) ``` ::: :::
